display.title: Marbin B'Simcha: Adding Joy When Adar Begins
display.summary_short: Why Adar calls not just for joy but for more joy: a simcha that grows from trusting that Hashem protects the Jewish people and foils every enemy's plans.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given the week of Shabbos Mevarchim Adar 5751. Uncle Yossi points out that the Sages do not say only 'be happy' in Adar, but 'marbin b'simcha', add and multiply the joy. A soldier in Tzivos Hashem already has a standing order to serve Hashem with joy all year, a joy that comes from firm belief that Hashem, the Guardian of Israel who never sleeps, protects us wherever we are. As we say in our prayers, 'Utzu eitzah vesufar... ki imanu Keil': whatever the enemies plan will come to nothing, for Hashem is with us. Adar is the month of miracles and of Haman's downfall, and Uncle Yossi prays that this year of wonders will bring a new holiday like Purim, celebrating the downfall of today's Hamans, and the coming of Moshiach, the king of peace.
display.lesson: When Adar comes, add to your joy, because Hashem is always with us and protects us.
